raw_segments.text: Under the old malt tax, indeed, is comprehended a tax of four shillings upon the hogshead
of cider, and another of ten shillings upon the barrel of mum.

It probably fell somewhat short of its usual amount, all the different taxes upon cider,
having that year produced less than ordinary.

But to balance whatever may be the ordinary amount of those two taxes, there is comprehended
under what is called the country excise.
First, the old excise of six shillings and eightpence upon the hogshead of cider.
Secondly, a like tax of six shillings and eightpence upon the hogshead of vergus.
Thirdly, another of eight shillings and ninepence upon the hogshead of vinegar.
And lastly, a fourth tax of elevenpence upon the gallon of mead or methagline.
The produce of those different taxes will probably much more than counterbalance that
of the duties imposed by what is called the annual malt tax upon cider and mum.
